schemaNotes: Cards never encode position or membership. The textbook holds both.

dataFields.note: title carries ONLY the description; the engine writes "Example N — "

bellringer.label: Bellringer
bellringer.purpose: Focus attention and pull prior learning out of memory before anything new arrives.

do-now.label: Do Now
do-now.purpose: A short task a learner can start alone, before instruction begins.
do-now.notes: Answerable from prior learning. If it needs today’s lesson it belongs in the lesson.

context-reading.label: Context Reading
context-reading.purpose: A real situation the day’s tool actually solves.
context-reading.notes: End on a question. A vignette that resolves itself hands over the insight and leaves nothing.

context-review.label: Context Review
context-review.purpose: Surface what the reading was about, before naming the mathematics.

retrieval.label: Spaced Retrieval
retrieval.purpose: Recall from an EARLIER lesson, not this one.
retrieval.notes: Ask for recall in a different format from the one it was taught in. Recapping in the same format is not retrieval.

primer.label: Lesson Primer
primer.purpose: Say what today is for, and put the vocabulary and tools within reach.

objective.label: Objective
objective.purpose: What a learner will be able to do, observably, by the end.

definitions.label: Definitions
definitions.purpose: The words this lesson uses, defined before they are used.
definitions.notes: Fully populated. Never a table with blanks to fill in during the lesson. A trap belongs here when it disambiguates notation rather than diagnosing a method error — misconceptions are cheapest to correct before they are used.

tools.label: Tools
tools.purpose: The rules and notation the lesson will apply.
tools.notes: A rule needs its one-line reason. A rule with nothing underneath it has a shelf life.

prerequisite-check.label: Prerequisite Check
prerequisite-check.purpose: Find where a learner should start.
prerequisite-check.notes: Tests prerequisites, never the lesson’s own objective.

lesson.label: Lesson
lesson.purpose: Show the method worked, then work it together.

lecture.label: Lecture
lecture.purpose: The explanation: where the rule comes from and why it holds.

modeling.label: Worked Examples
modeling.purpose: A full solution, method selection visible.
modeling.notes: Full worked examples, not partial. For fragmented prior knowledge the worked-example effect outweighs completion tasks.

trap.label: Common Trap
trap.purpose: A named misconception, diagnosed rather than warned against.
trap.notes: Correct misconceptions early. An uncorrected error gets reinforced.

structured-practice.label: Structured Practice
structured-practice.purpose: Guided attempt with the scaffold still present.

practice.label: Practice and Check for Understanding
practice.purpose: Independent work, and evidence of whether it landed.

error-analysis.label: Error Analysis
error-analysis.notes: The one item type that only works when the answer is visible.

flashcards.label: Flashcards
flashcards.purpose: Recall of terms and rules, spaced.
flashcards.notes: Correct cards space out; missed cards come back sooner (Leitner).

checkpoint.label: Checkpoint
checkpoint.purpose: A low-stakes check the learner can act on.

exit.label: Exit Ticket
exit.purpose: Retrieval, not a summary. Generation, not recognition.

retrieval-check.label: Retrieval Check
retrieval-check.purpose: Recall today’s work from memory, notes closed.
retrieval-check.notes: “What was the main idea?” demands almost nothing. “Without looking, explain why …” demands genuine retrieval.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.purpose: What the learner noticed about their own thinking.

confidence.label: Confidence
confidence.notes: Captured, never used to gate anything.

looking-ahead.label: Looking Ahead
looking-ahead.notes: Written by the engine from the textbook order. Authors do not supply it.

conditional.title: required for refresher, rule, example, trap, handoff

optional.requires: array of card ids this card cannot be read without. Validated at the TEXTBOOK layer.
optional.scope: library (default) | textbook-only | lesson-only. Records where a card was BORN.

complexity.note: House vocabulary. Never easy or hard, including in comments.

standards.note: Tag honestly. Inflating everything to lesson makes coverage reports worthless.

topic.note: A SEARCH FACET. It does not decide which chapter a card lands in — the textbook does.

hourglass.scope: within topic; a two-topic lesson keeps topics contiguous

crossReferences.note: Never write "the example above". Unresolvable ids render as a visible [missing reference: id].

fractions.note: Write fractional coordinates as strings, e.g. "3/2". No entity is required.

engineOwned: the word Example and its number

entities.note: Use these, not literal characters. A plain hyphen looks right and hashes differently.

vocabulary.note: Use essential/complex. Multiplicative inverse language: multiply by 1/15, never divide by 15.

textbookChanges.note: Two shapes. Supply whichever applies; both may be absent.
textbookChanges.topics: [{id, title?, subtitle?, cards:[ids in order]}] — edits to the BOOK
textbookChanges.lessons: [{day, slug, title, sections:[{id,title,phase,cards}]}] — edits to a LESSON
textbookChanges.semantics: A supplied card list REPLACES that container entirely. List every card you want kept.

workShapes.note: data.work on example and practice cards takes ONE of two shapes. Never mix keys.

solve.goal: the unknowns, each defined with := ("h := the rise, in inches")
solve.facts: array; each entry [quote, math] (a given as written, then the math it becomes) or a plain string
solve.steps: array of {find?, math}: one step per unknown, in solving order; find is plain words
solve.answer: the result on its own line
solve.labels: none by default (reads as a textbook solution); render cfg.workLabels = "process" prints Goal, Facts, 5 or 5a/5b..., Answer
